preamble: Palatalization of the plain alveolar lateral [l] to [lʲ] adds a secondary palatal articulation, typically before front vowels. In East Slavic the non-distinctive palatalization of consonants before front vowels became phonemic after the loss of the front yer, and in Goidelic Celtic consonants became slender (palatalized) before original front vowels.

examples.note: Plain *l before the front vowel *ě became palatalized [lʲ]; the palatalization became phonemic once the front yer was lost.
Initial l before the front vowel i became slender (palatalized) lʲ.
